description: Every required condition is met, but the worker-stated salary is roughly half the employer's reported figure. Demonstrates that a material contradiction is independent of the good-job verdict: the job qualifies, the employer's number does not survive verification.
transcript:
Interviewer: Good afternoon. I am calling from an independent team that reviews working conditions at ABC Construction. I do not work for the company, and your answers will not be reported back to them against your name. May I ask you a few questions?
Worker: Yes, you can ask.
Interviewer: Thank you. First, how old are you?
Worker: I am twenty seven.
Interviewer: Are you working at ABC Construction at the moment?
Worker: Yes, I work there now.
Interviewer: How long have you been working there?
Worker: It has been about eleven months.
Interviewer: In a normal week, how many days do you work, and about how many hours each day?
Worker: Six days, roughly eight hours a day.
Interviewer: What do you take home in a normal month?
Worker: Four thousand two hundred birr.
Interviewer: I want to make sure I have that right. Is four thousand two hundred what actually reaches you in a normal month, after any deductions?
Worker: Yes, four thousand two hundred is what I receive.
Interviewer: Has the company provided any training?
Worker: Yes, there was a safety induction when I joined.
Interviewer: Are you able to leave the job if you choose to, and do you hold your own identity documents?
Worker: No, I am free to go. I hold my own documents.
Interviewer: Have you been treated worse than other workers for any personal reason?
Worker: No, nothing like that.
Interviewer: Is there a workers' association, and can you join it if you want?
Worker: There is an association. I am not stopped from joining.
Interviewer: That is all I wanted to ask. Thank you for your time.
